chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Fasting is obligatory upon the boy when he reaches puberty, and fasting and the headscarf (khimar) are obligatory upon the girl when she menstruates, unless she is a slave girl, for there is no headscarf upon her unless she wishes to wear it, and fasting is upon her.
ai.seo_question: When do fasting and headscarf become obligatory for boys and girls in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific biological markers of *bulugh* (puberty) for determining religious accountability (*taklif*), linking fasting obligations to seminal emission in boys and menstruation in girls. It further clarifies the ruling on the headscarf (*khimar*), noting that while it is recommended for free girls, it is not obligatory for slave girls unless they choose to wear it, highlighting the nuanced application of modesty laws in classical Shia jurisprudence. The narration underscores the transition from childhood innocence to full legal responsibility in Shia fiqh, serving as a foundational text for understanding the onset of obligatory acts.
